_partNote: Genomics is full of flat rectangles, so the six tiles are pushed apart by form factor: a wide flat lane-striped slide (short read), a waisted pore in a membrane strip (long read), a small square dot-grid chip (targeted and legacy), a circle inside a circle (single cell and spatial), a lidded cone (sample prep), and a narrow upright cylinder (writing DNA). The flow cell and the array are the pair to watch — one is wide and striped with parallel lanes, the other is square and covered in a fine regular dot grid.

partPrompts.1: A sequencing flow cell lying flat, seen three-quarter: a thin wide rectangular glass slide, clearly much wider than it is deep and only a few millimeters thick, its top face divided along its length into eight straight parallel lanes separated by fine ruled lines, with a small round port at each end of every lane. Low, flat and distinctly landscape. One object only, lying on a plain surface; no instrument, no housing, no tray, no dot grid, no vessel and no equipment.
partPrompts.2: A single protein nanopore set in a thin flat membrane, seen three-quarter in section from the side: a squat barrel-shaped body noticeably pinched to a narrow waist at its middle so the silhouette reads as an hourglass, seated through a thin flat horizontal sheet that extends a short way to either side of it like a shelf, with one slender strand entering the top opening and a short length of the same strand emerging below the bottom opening. The waisted barrel is the subject and the sheet is a plain thin line. One pore only; no other pores, no array, no lanes, no grid, no vessel and no equipment.
partPrompts.3: A genotyping microarray chip lying flat, seen three-quarter: a small square wafer, as deep as it is wide, its entire top face covered edge to edge in a fine regular grid of identical small round dots in evenly spaced rows and columns, set into a plain square frame with a narrow flat border all around. Square and evenly textured. One object only, lying on a plain surface; no lanes, no stripes, no parallel channels, no ports, no instrument, no vessel and no equipment.
partPrompts.4: A single spherical droplet drawn large and centered with generous empty margins on every side, seen three-quarter: a clear round bead with a smooth unbroken outline and a soft curved highlight near its upper left, holding one smaller sphere suspended slightly below and left of its center that reads plainly as a cell. Drawn as dimensional line art with the rounded shading of a glass bead, never as a flat graphic. One droplet only, complete and well inside the frame. No second droplet, nothing cropped or touching the frame edges, no face, no eyes, no channels, no tubing, no chip, no straight lines anywhere, no vessel and no equipment.
partPrompts.5: A microcentrifuge tube standing upright, seen three-quarter: a smooth tapered body narrowing from a wide mouth to a rounded point at the bottom so the silhouette is a clean cone, with a flat rim around the top, a small hinged lid standing open and tipped back on its short hinge tab, and a shallow pool of liquid resting in the bottom of the cone. Small, conical, and clearly a single tube. One object only; not a rack, no other tubes, no straight-sided cylinder, no instrument, no vessel and no equipment.
partPrompts.6: A small DNA synthesis cartridge standing upright, seen three-quarter: a short stubby opaque molded-plastic barrel only about twice as tall as it is wide, with a narrow cone-shaped luer fitting projecting from the center of the top and an identical one from the center of the bottom, each ending in a small round opening, and an even fine packing filling the barrel between two thin discs. Small, squat and obviously injection-molded plastic. One object only; no flanges, no wide rims, no collars, no glass, no transparent walls, no metal end caps, nothing tall or slender, no vessel and no equipment.
